newsitem.title: UK: Australia streaks ahead in govt bond index - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Australia streaks ahead in govt bond index - Salomon.

text.p: Australian bonds left the field standing in the Salomon world government bond index (WGBI) in the week to July 10, Salomon Brothers said on Friday.

Overall the WGBI gained 0.29 percent in local currency terms in a week that saw just Ireland and the UK make negative returns. The index rose by the same amount in dollar terms in an overall stable week for the U.S. dollar.

Australian government bonds rallied 1.51 percent in Australian dollars on the back of rate cut expectations. Lower-than-expected June unemployment data came in at 8.5 percent, down from 8.8 percent in May.
During the week the Bank of England increased base interest rates by 25 basis points to 6.75 percent. Gilts fell by 0.6 percent in pounds. Irish bonds dropped 0.3 percent in punts.

Canada trailed Australia, gaining 0.45 percent in Canadian dollars, rising higher in the slipstream of firm U.S. Treasuries. Canadian bonds have strengthened since the U.S. Federal Reserve opted to leave interest rates unchanged at its July 2 policy-setting meeting. Treasuries gained 0.41 percent.
Italian government bonds gained 0.43 percent in lire after positive EMU sentiment saw further yield convergence.
The BTP/Bund yield on Monday breached psychological resistance at 100 basis points, and by Thursday had forged its way to 94 bp.
German government bonds rose 0.20 percent in marks, while French government bonds gained 0.40 percent in francs.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
